proposals.observation: 10 sessions landed on the quiz intro in 48 hours; 0 started, 0 completed. Every user stalled at intro_load and left. This is a copy or CTA friction problem on the first visible screen — not a traffic problem.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the quiz intro headline and sub-copy to make the first action feel low-stakes and grounded. The current framing likely positions the quiz as a test or a label, which triggers avoidance in the ICP. Replace with language that frames it as a quiet moment of honest reckoning — something you do for yourself, not a score you receive. Also replace any generic CTA button text (e.g. 'Start Quiz' or 'Begin') with a phrase that lowers the threshold.
proposals.new_text: Take an honest look — it takes 3 minutes
proposals.impact: Converts stalled intro sessions into quiz starts

proposals.observation: The 'Daily Blog Post' GitHub Actions workflow failed at 06:21 on 2026-05-12. The content queue shows only 1 post queued and 0 published in the last 24 hours. The pipeline is broken, meaning the blog is silently going dark — a direct hit to organic discovery and ICP trust-building.
proposals.proposal: Inspect the workflow run logs and fix the root cause. Most likely culprits are an expired API key (OpenAI or similar), a missing environment secret, or a schema mismatch in the generated frontmatter. Add a fallback step that opens a GitHub Issue on failure so the break surfaces immediately rather than silently. As an immediate patch, manually publish the 1 queued post today so the content cadence does not slip.
proposals.new_text:
- name: Notify on failure
  if: failure()
  uses: actions/github-script@v7
  with:
    script: |
      github.rest.issues.create({
        owner: context.repo.owner,
        repo: context.repo.repo,
        title: 'Daily Blog Post workflow failed – ' + new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10),
        body: 'Workflow run failed. Check logs: ' + context.serverUrl + '/' + context.repo.owner + '/' + context.repo.repo + '/actions/runs/' + context.runId
      })
proposals.impact: Surfaces pipeline failures immediately; stops content cadence going dark

proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has the highest open rate at 50% (4/8 opens) — well above Money Avoidance (40%) and Money Worship (37.5%). Vigilance profiles in the ICP — people who earn well but don't build — are the closest match to Joel's core customer. Yet this sequence has the smallest send volume (8) versus Avoidance (15) and Worship (16), suggesting fewer quiz completers are being routed into it, or the quiz isn't completing enough to route anyone. The high open rate signals the copy already resonates; the constraint is reach, not quality.
proposals.proposal: Add a standalone 'Money Vigilance' blog post pitched directly at the story beneath that profile — the quiet, steady earner who tracks everything but can't make a move. This requires no workflow change, no quiz fix, and ships as a single markdown file. The post should surface organically and also serve as a manual entry point to the Vigilance sequence for anyone Joel links to directly (e.g. in a social post or newsletter). Target the honest reckoning framing: 'You know your numbers. So why won't you do anything with them?'
proposals.new_text:
---
title: "You know your numbers. So why won't you act on them?"
pubDate: 2026-05-13
description: "A quiet look at what sits underneath careful tracking and careful inaction — and what it costs to keep watching without moving."
tags: ["money vigilance", "the work underneath", "honest reckoning"]
---

You are not someone who ignores money. You check the account. You read the statements. You have probably built a spreadsheet or two.

And yet — nothing moves.

Not because you don't know what to do. You do. Not because you can't afford to. You probably can. But there is something underneath the watching that the watching itself keeps you from having to look at.

This is the pattern that rarely gets named: the person who is careful, grounded, on top of things — and completely stuck.

It is worth turning toward that gap. Not to fix it in an afternoon, but to understand what the caution is actually protecting. Because careful and cautious are not the same thing, and one of them is costing you more than you have accounted for yet.

If this feels familiar, the [money beliefs quiz](/quiz) takes about three minutes and asks some of the questions that are easier to answer in private.
proposals.impact: Creates organic SEO and social entry point for highest-converting audience segment
